content.value_statement: Manual changelog updates are easy to miss and hard to standardize. This skill helps teams build repeatable release notes from commits, PRs, and versions.
actual_capabilities: Explains Keep a Changelog structure and release section conventions.
Maps Conventional Commit types to changelog categories.
Provides setup patterns for commitlint, husky, standard-version, semantic-release, git-cliff, and commitizen.
Shows GitHub Actions workflow patterns for automated releases.
Includes public and internal release notes templates.
limitations: It does not run release tools by itself.
Examples must be adapted to each repository, package manager, and registry.
It does not verify branch protection, token scope, or registry permissions.
Output quality depends on consistent commit messages and PR metadata.

use_cases.title: Set Up Release Automation
use_cases.description: Create a repeatable workflow for changelog generation, version bumps, tags, and release notes.

use_cases.title: Adopt Commit Standards
use_cases.description: Define Conventional Commit rules and map commit types to changelog sections.

use_cases.title: Prepare Release Notes
use_cases.description: Turn completed features, fixes, and dependency updates into clear release summaries.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Changelog
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use changelog-automation to draft a Keep a Changelog outline for this project. Include Unreleased, Added, Changed, Fixed, and Security sections.

prompt_templates.title: Map Commit Types
prompt_templates.prompt: Use changelog-automation to define Conventional Commit types for our team. Explain which types should appear in release notes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Release Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use changelog-automation to recommend a release workflow for a Node.js package. Include commit validation, changelog generation, and manual approval points.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Existing Process
prompt_templates.prompt: Use changelog-automation to review our current release process. Identify gaps in commit standards, changelog quality, token permissions, and release review controls.

output_examples.input: We need a changelog format for a library that ships monthly releases.
output: A recommended changelog with Unreleased, Added, Changed, Fixed, and Security sections.
A release entry format that includes dates, versions, issue references, and compare links.
Guidance for keeping breaking changes visible before each release.

output_examples.input: Our team wants release notes from Conventional Commits.
output: A mapping from feature, fix, performance, revert, and refactor commits into release note sections.
A recommendation to hide routine docs, style, test, build, and chore commits unless they affect users.
A validation plan using commit message rules before merge.

output_examples.input: Review our automated publishing workflow before we enable it.
output: A checklist for branch protection, manual approval, token scope, and dry-run testing.
A warning to confirm package registry permissions before automatic publishing.
A recommendation to review generated release notes before public release.

best_practices: Use Conventional Commits consistently before relying on automated changelog generation.
Review generated release notes before publishing packages or creating public releases.
Keep release credentials scoped to the minimum permissions required.
anti_patterns: Mixing unrelated changes in one commit or pull request.
Publishing releases automatically from unprotected branches.
Editing generated changelog entries without updating the release workflow.

faq.question: Does this skill generate a changelog automatically?
faq.answer: It provides patterns and templates for automation. The user must run or configure the selected release tool.

faq.question: Which changelog format does it follow?
faq.answer: It centers on Keep a Changelog and maps Conventional Commit types to readable sections.

faq.question: Can it support GitHub Releases?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes GitHub Actions and release note template patterns that can be adapted.

faq.question: Can it support Python projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes commitizen patterns for version bumps and changelog updates in Python projects.

faq.question: Does it decide semantic versions?
faq.answer: It explains how breaking changes, features, and fixes map to major, minor, and patch releases.

faq.question: What should teams review before using automation?
faq.answer: Teams should review branch protection, token scope, registry access, and generated release notes.
